headline: Overdose prevention centers, Boston's sharps disposal ordinance, and Eversource gas leak reports.
summary: A petition for community clothing closets near Woo Fridges is also on the agenda. Several items are orders from councilors, including a review of stroke and dementia rates in a downtown census tract.
items: Communication from the City Manager on the Office of New Americans
Petition to install Community Clothing Closets near Woo Fridges to provide weather-appropriate clothing
Order to review why a downtown census tract has the highest rate of stroke and dementia in Massachusetts for Medicare residents 65 and older
Order to review and discuss Boston's ordinance on safe disposal of sharps through a product stewardship program
Order asking the City Manager to get a report from Eversource on grade 1, 2, and 3 gas leaks over the past five years
Order to invite the Office of New Americans to discuss support for refugees and new arrivals
Chairman's order to meet jointly with the Board of Health for a presentation by Dr. Brandon Marshall on overdose prevention centers and safe injection sites
location: Esther Howland (South) Chamber, City Hall, 455 Main Street, Worcester, Massachusetts

a.
Important Notice: Residents are advised of an ongoing scam involving the impersonation 
of city officials and departments. Scammers are fraudulently requesting payments be made 
for planning and zoning permits, as well as City Council petitions. All official emails 
regarding your petition will come exclusively from an @worcesterma.gov email address 
(such as clerk @worcesterma.gov), or via physical mail on the City of Worcester’s official 
letterhead. Any legitimate hearing letter will always include your specific application 
details, along with the scheduled hearing date, time, and location. The City of Worcester 
will never request payments via wire transfer.
